f1.leadTitle: Volume growth is real; the customer, the technology and the order book all lean on others
takeaways: FY26 revenue was ₹2,312 cr (+28%) and PAT ₹180 cr. Q1 FY27 deliveries rose to 358 buses (+122%). FY27 guide: 2,500 buses.

Most buses are sold to Evey Trans SPVs, owned by the promoter MEIL. Evey runs them for state transport bodies under 12-year GCC contracts, so Olectra gets paid only after Evey's bank debt is drawn and state subsidies arrive. BEST has paid subsidy on 10 of 686 buses; Maharashtra owes Evey about ₹860 cr.

~6,000 of the ~8,000-bus order book (MSRTC ~4,000, BEST ~2,000) is 'neither cancelled nor accepted'. At ₹951 (44x TTM) it is a paper HOLD with a ₹1,123 weighted target; reward:risk is 0.75x (unfavourable).

sources: FY26 results and AGM notice (26 Sep 2026)
ICRA and India Ratings (22 May 2026) rationales

topInsights: The order book is smaller than it looks: ~6,000 of ~8,000 buses are MSRTC/BEST orders that are 'neither cancelled nor accepted'. Clean orders are ~2,000 buses, about one year of FY27 guidance.
Olectra's credit risk is the promoter's: Evey (MEIL) buys the buses and pays only when its banks lend and states pay. Maharashtra owes Evey ~₹860 cr; FCF has been negative for 2 years.
Costs are ~85% variable, so margins hold but EPS moves with volume. 82% of the price is a growth bet, while reward:risk is 0.75x.

f2.leadTitle: STRESSED: related-party concentration and stuck order book, not solvency
takeaways: REDs: 1.2 FCF negative 2 yrs; 2.2 receivables tied to stuck subsidies; 2.3 Evey (MEIL) is the main buyer; 6.4 ~75% of the order book disputed; 7.3 related-party sales well above 5%.
Solvency is fine: debt ≈1.1x EBITDA, ICR ~4.4x, IND A/Stable (upgraded May 2026), ICRA positive outlook.
It flips to WATCH if the MSRTC schedule is signed and Maharashtra clears Evey's subsidy dues.

sources: FY26 results and AGM notice (26 Sep 2026)
ICRA and India Ratings (22 May 2026) rationales

f2.combinedVerdict: STRESSED on related-party and order-book risk, not fraud: Schilit flags a related buyer and consolidation cut-outs; Mulford shows CFO/EBITDA falling to 46% and FCF negative; solvency is fine (ICR ~4.4x, IND A/Stable). Insider lens: REC LOC contingent fell from ₹272 cr to nil, but a ₹300 cr advance undertaking replaced it; warranty reserve is adequate (₹43 cr, 1.9% of sales); ₹13.7 cr of capitalised interest. Tice lens (FY26 annual report): payables funded 167% of FY25–26 standalone OCF, and 66% of FY26 payables were past due (₹486 cr vs ₹154 cr); short-seller call WATCH.

literature: Forced CEO exits follow poor performance, and announcement returns are small and ambiguous (Warner, Watts & Wruck 1988). Firms that hire an outsider CEO tend to see operating performance improve afterwards (Huson, Malatesta & Parrino 2004). So treat a 'star hire' as a slow-acting signal, not a quick price rerating.

CFOs are more likely to be replaced after poor performance (Mian 2001). Executive departures, CFOs included, cluster around financial restatements (e.g. Arthaud-Day et al. 2006). A sudden, unexplained CFO exit is a forensic red flag; Olectra has had none.

Employee satisfaction is priced slowly. 'Best Companies to Work For' earned about 2.3–3.8% a year of alpha, 1984–2009 (Edmans 2011). Improving Glassdoor ratings predict higher future returns (Green, Huang, Wen & Zhou 2019). Olectra's ratings are flat to low and attrition is rising, which is a mild negative.

narratives: E-bus demand is real, but rivals are taking it. India's e-bus sales rose 55% to 3,723 in Apr–Sep 2026; penetration is 8.55% (x.com/gaze_observer/status/2107341713199206819). JBM took 33% of September registrations (x.com/_Investor_Feed_/status/2105574791545757973). PM e-Drive has 14,000 buses allotted (x.com/JulehMobility/status/2103680960902676969).

Rates and valuations weigh on auto stocks. With the RBI hiking, posts warn that expensive auto names could correct more (x.com/stocksbyrishabh/status/2109460294305288590). Nifty Auto is down about 8% over a year (x.com/SwingAcumen/status/2113862758680936842). Strong October sales gave only a one-day bounce (x.com/RisingIndiaHQ/status/2117106147882897885).

Policy friction and China. The traction-motor localisation deadline was pushed to April 2027 because China has not granted rare-earth magnet licences (x.com/snipy_in/status/2096194914057142399). PM e-Drive e-truck subsidies reached only 52 of 5,643 trucks by 24 Aug (x.com/lakshmishaks/status/2094420920438051238). The China EV/BYD read-across was not checked (gap).

f10.methodDetail: Reward : risk = median % upside of scenarios above the price ÷ median % downside of those below. Rule: ≥1.5x favourable, 0.8–1.5x balanced, below 0.8x unfavourable. 'Marker' rows are shown on the ladder but excluded from the ratio. Technical prices: Yahoo Finance NSE daily closes to 30 Oct 2026. Fundamental rows are estimates (EST). Near-duplicate lenses (DCF variants, ATR/volatility bands, 50/200-DMA, swing pivots, EV/EBITDA bands, revenue shocks already on the Cost tab, thin peer sets) were removed because they move together and add no new information. Value is imprecise: these are ways to think about where the price could go, not forecasts. Paper analysis only, not advice.

f16.leadTitle: Stakeholder lens: 2 RED (customers, competitors), 4 AMBER, 1 GREEN, 1 NO DATA. Stakeholder-adjusted P/E ~29x vs 44x (−15 turns, capped, EST)
takeaways: Customers: related-party buyer Evey; PMPML ₹55 cr breakdown fine; ~75% of the order book on hold.
Competitors: share 23.5% → 19.6% (FY26) → 9.5% (H1 2026); CESL per-km price war.
Hidden: FDSS/safety compliance, plus contingent undertakings to Evey's lenders. Not advice.

sources: FY26 results and AGM notice (26 Sep 2026)
ICRA and India Ratings (22 May 2026) rationales

f16.stripBanner: STAKEHOLDER STRIP · base P/E ~44x · EST, not advice
f16.adjustedMultiple: Stakeholder-adjusted multiple (EST): sum of impacts -20x, capped at -15x → ~29x P/E (≈-34%). The impacts overlap (customers, regulator and competitors share causes), hence the cap.
topHiddenRisks: Market-share collapse to 9.5% in H1 2026 amid per-km price wars.
Safety/regulatory: FDSS non-compliance, the PMPML ₹55 cr fine and blacklisting threat, and the BEST accident audit demand.
Undertakings to Evey's lenders: contingent leverage tied to state payers.

lenses.name: Government / policy
lenses.who: MHI (PM e-Drive), CESL, state transport bodies (STUs)
lenses.evidence: PM e-Drive: 14,028 e-buses with a ₹4,391 cr outlay; grant = lowest of ₹10k/kWh, ₹35 lakh cap, or 20% of capital cost, paid 20/30/25/25 by milestone (CESL RfP). Olectra/Evey won 1,785 of 10,900 in Phase 1 (Mint). Maharashtra owes Evey ~₹860 cr; BEST has paid subsidy on only 10 of 686 buses (Q1 FY27 call). Promoter MEIL: ~₹966 cr of electoral bonds; CBI FIR Apr 2024.
lenses.hiddenRisk: Demand is policy-made and paid out by cash-poor states. The 75% of the grant paid after operations start means buses that don't run earn no subsidy. Political ties cut both ways after a change of government.

lenses.name: Regulator / safety
lenses.who: SEBI/NSE, MCA, GST, ARAI/MoRTH (CMVR, AIS-135), STU safety audits
lenses.evidence: 50 new BEST e-buses parked without the mandatory fire detection and suppression system (FDSS, AIS-135) (PTI, Jun 2025). Pune Olectra bus fire, Sep 2024 (compressor/short circuit; the auto-suppression failed). BEST: 16 major incidents May–Jun 2026; activists want an independent audit of contractor-run Olectra buses (FPJ). DATA GAP: no SEBI/MCA/GST orders found.
lenses.hiddenRisk: A formal MoRTH/ARAI safety audit or recall would hit the whole installed fleet and future tender eligibility, not just one city.

lenses.name: Customers
lenses.who: Evey (MEIL SPVs) as buyer; end users are STUs (MSRTC, BEST, PMPML, TGSRTC) and commuters
lenses.evidence: Most buses go to related party Evey; ~75% of the order book (MSRTC ~4,000 + BEST ~2,000) is on hold. PMPML fined Olectra ₹55 cr after 45 battery breakdowns in 45 days, ordered cell replacement on 25 buses at Olectra's cost, and threatened blacklisting (HT, Sep 2025). Debtor days 156.
lenses.hiddenRisk: Service failures turn into penalties under GCC contracts and reputation loss across STUs that talk to each other. The real customer (the STU) has no switching cost at the next tender.

lenses.name: Suppliers
lenses.who: BYD (technology licence), cell makers (China), FDSS/component vendors
lenses.evidence: BYD technology licence; LFP cells imported (EST, likely China). Next-gen platform with a local battery slipped to Q4 FY27 (F11). PM e-Drive requires minimum domestic value addition (phased manufacturing programme). Payable days 153; LC limits ₹935 cr.
lenses.hiddenRisk: A geopolitical or duty shock on Chinese cells, or BYD terms changing, hits both cost and subsidy eligibility. Delayed FDSS supply already stalled deliveries.

lenses.name: Employees
lenses.evidence: Permanent-employee turnover 35% → 37.9% → 52% (BRSR FY24–26). AmbitionBox 3.3, culture 2.8; Glassdoor 3.3, senior management 2.9. 0 permanent workers. Details in F4.
lenses.hiddenRisk: Service quality (breakdowns, FDSS fits) depends on a churning, contract-heavy workforce. This links to lens 3.

lenses.name: Lenders / capital
lenses.who: Banks (LC, term loans), ICRA, India Ratings, Evey's lenders
lenses.evidence: IND A/Stable (upgraded May 2026); ICRA positive outlook. Debt ₹380 cr ≈ 1.1x EBITDA. AGM Sep 2026 approved undertakings to Evey lenders and MEIL guarantees/loans. CareEdge: GCC bankability depends on payment security, escrow and DSRA, and STUs paying on time.
lenses.hiddenRisk: The undertakings to Evey lenders are effectively contingent, off-balance-sheet leverage tied to state payers. DATA GAP: amount.

lenses.name: Community & environment
lenses.who: Plant locality (Telangana), regulators for battery waste/EPR, ESG investors
lenses.evidence: BRSR FY26 filed but not assured (assurance: NA). DATA GAP: Battery Waste Management Rules EPR registration and recycling volumes, plant land/approval disputes. Positive: e-bus lifecycle cost ~15–20% below AC diesel (CareEdge).
lenses.hiddenRisk: Battery end-of-life liability grows as the 2019-era fleet ages (Pune buses already past 5 years).

lenses.name: Competitors / entrants
lenses.who: Switch, JBM, PMI, EKA/Pinnacle, Tata, VECV
lenses.evidence: Olectra share 23.5% (FY25) → 19.6% (FY26, 853 units) → 9.5% (H1 2026, 4th; Switch 28.2%) (Vahan via BusinessLine, Sustainable Bus). CESL Phase 1: PMI 5,210, EKA 3,485, Olectra 1,785; per-km rates 'lower than estimates', some bids ₹5–18/km apart (Mint, ETAuto). Top 4 capacity ~32,000/yr vs 2026 market ~6,000.
lenses.hiddenRisk: Overcapacity plus per-km price wars squeeze Evey's economics, which then pushes on Olectra's bus price. 'Pioneer' status no longer wins tenders.

f16.wantsNote: What each stakeholder wants: Government wants cheap, reliable buses with local content. Regulators want safety compliance. STUs want uptime at a low per-km fee. Suppliers want volume. Employees want stability and growth. Lenders want escrowed cash flows. Community wants clean air and safe battery disposal. Rivals want share. Sources: CESL PM e-Drive RfP; Mint/ETAuto (Dec 2025); Hindu BusinessLine, Sustainable Bus (Vahan); CareEdge e-bus report (2026); Hindustan Times, Indian Express, TOI, PTI, Free Press Journal; BRSR FY26; earlier tabs. Multiples are judgemental estimates (EST). DATA GAPs are flagged.
